title: Unauthenticated email-change ATO (djoser reset_email)
summary: Prove JWT skip on reset_email / reset_email_confirm with a 401 sibling vs 204 canary. Do not complete ATO on a real mailbox.
steps: Map POST /api/auth/users/reset_email/, reset_email_confirm/, and set_password/ from OpenAPI or crawl.
Baseline: unauth POST set_password (or another account-mod). Expect 401.
Mutant: unauth POST reset_email with email=aegis-ato-canary@example.invalid. Expect 204/200.
Then unauth POST reset_email_confirm uid=MQ (base64 user 1) + garbage token. 'Invalid token for given user' vs 'Invalid user id' enumerates users. 2–4 uids max.
PASS: sibling 401 AND reset_email accepted without a session. OPTIONS 401 or schema jwtAuth is NOT a kill.
One canary email. Do not complete ATO on a production mailbox. Do not spray employee inboxes.
pass_signals: Unauth reset_email returns 204/200 while set_password returns 401
reset_email_confirm locates a user without a session
kill_signals: Both email-change endpoints return 401/403 like set_password
